cards.text: After this, the Lord appoints seventy-two others and sends them ahead of Him to every town and place He's about to visit. SEVENTY-TWO! I've got six stations, and some mornings I still can't find my own apron.

cards.question: Jesus sends the seventy-two out one at a time, each one on his own.

cards.text: Before they go, Jesus gives them a picture: ‘The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.’ Big job. Short staff. Every adult with a job just nodded.

cards.question: With a big harvest and only a few workers, what does Jesus tell the seventy-two to do?

answers.text: Ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers
Work harder to bring in what they can
Wait until more workers show up first

cards.text: Then Jesus says, ‘Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.’ No fine print, friend. He puts it right on the front of the box.

cards.question: With that picture of lambs among wolves, Jesus is telling the seventy-two this trip will be safe and easy.

cards.text: Now the packing list, and first up: do not greet anyone along the road. Friend, I once chatted with a rubber band in that junk drawer for THREE HOURS, so I would not make it.

cards.question: What does Jesus tell the seventy-two not to carry?

answers.text: A purse or bag or sandals
A staff or cloak or tunic
A lamp or scroll or blanket

cards.text: Whatever house they walk into, Jesus tells them to begin with these words: ‘Peace to this house.’ Not ‘Hey.’ Not ‘Nice place.’ PEACE.

cards.question: The seventy-two say ‘Peace to this house.’ If no man of peace is there, what happens to that peace?

answers.text: It stays on the house anyway

cards.text: Once they're welcomed into a house, Jesus says eat and drink whatever they're offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two to move to a new house every night so no one family carries the load.
When a town welcomes the seventy-two, they eat whatever is set before them. What else does Jesus send them to do there?

answers.text: Heal the sick and tell them God's kingdom is near
Teach the law and settle all their disputes
Gather the people and collect an offering

cards.text: But if a town doesn't welcome them, they go into the streets and declare, ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you.’ Friend, I spent years under junk drawer dust, and nobody EVER wiped me off that dramatically.

cards.question: Even to a town that won't welcome them, the seventy-two still declare, ‘Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is ___.’

cards.text: Jesus says that on that day, it will be more bearable for Sodom than for that town. Then He calls out two towns by name: ‘Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida!’

cards.question: Jesus says if the miracles performed in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, those cities would have ___ long ago.

cards.text: Jesus says it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for those towns. Then He calls out one more: ‘And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven?’

cards.question: Jesus tells Capernaum it will be lifted up to heaven.
Jesus tells the seventy-two that whoever listens to them listens to Him, and whoever rejects them rejects Him. Who else does that person reject?

cards.text: Mission over, and the seventy-two come back to Jesus. Friend, they've got NEWS, and they cannot wait to tell it.

cards.question: What do the seventy-two tell Jesus when they get back?

answers.text: Even the demons submit to them in His name
The dead were raised in every town
Fire fell from heaven at their word

cards.question: The seventy-two come back from their trip discouraged and worn out.

cards.text: Jesus answers them, ‘I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.’ One sentence. Hits like thunder.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two He has given them authority over all the power of the enemy.

cards.text: Jesus tells them nothing will harm them. Then He says, ‘Nevertheless,’ and friend, when somebody says nevertheless, the whole conversation is about to turn around.

cards.question: Jesus tells the seventy-two not to rejoice that the spirits submit to them. What should they rejoice about instead?

answers.text: That their names are written in heaven
That every town will remember them
That they will see greater miracles

cards.text: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit. He declares, ‘I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth.’

cards.question: Jesus praises the Father for hiding these things from the wise and learned and revealing them to ___.
Jesus says all things have been entrusted to Him by His Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to the disciples and says privately, ‘Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.’

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that many people wanted to see what they see and hear what they hear, but never did. Who?

cards.text: Prophets and kings wanted it and never got it, and these disciples are standing right in the middle of it. Friend, I waited years in that junk drawer for one little slice of kitchen light, and they got the WHOLE sunrise.

findings.problem: The passage opens with 'After this,' mid-flow from Luke 9, but the opening card gives no context for what came before. It also never says that 'the Lord' is Jesus, so the baker isn't told who is speaking. Later cards switch to 'Jesus' without that ever being set up.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The core action is appointing and sending out a big team. The comparison is Papa Dorin losing his own apron, which isn't the same action. The joke doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Only the right answer uses the passage's Bible phrasing ('the Lord of the harvest') and picks up the harvest picture from card 3. Both wrong answers are plain modern work advice, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card treats 'this trip will be safe' as false. But in Luke 10:19 Jesus tells the seventy-two 'Nothing will harm you,' so a baker could argue for True using the passage itself.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The card says 'first up: do not greet anyone along the road.' In Luke 10:4, the command to carry no purse, bag or sandals comes first. The card also calls the greeting command part of a 'packing list,' which it isn't.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer-days event: a three-hour chat with a rubber band. Jokes may only invent small moments around his bakery. The drawer is part of the fixed backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This card is a near-verbatim reading of Luke 10:7 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: 'They've got NEWS, and they cannot wait to tell it' already rules out the 'discouraged and worn out' option, so card 3 is given away before it's asked.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Satan appears here for the first time with no simple word on who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card is a near-verbatim reading of Luke 10:21 with none of Papa Dorin's voice, at a moment of Jesus's joy that could carry it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The second half of Luke 10:22 is never told on any card: no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him. That's a key detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card is a near-verbatim reading of Luke 10:23 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card restates Luke 10:24, which card 12 just asked and answered. It adds no new piece of the passage and works as a recap with a joke on it.
